name: Yellow-crowned Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Southwestern costa rica to northern bolivia, the guianas, and amazonian brazil
description: Small, small-billed flycatcher usually found in the canopy. Yellow belly with gray head and pale whitish eyebrow.

name: Buff-cheeked Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Central amazonian brazil (madeira drainage in amazonas and rondônia)
description: Very small, poorly-known flycatcher. Note the buff lores and streaked throat.

name: Chattering Cisticola
rangeDescription: Nigeria to cameroon, gabon, congo, democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern angola
description: A common, nondescript bird found near the ground in grassy areas in fields, in towns, along roads, and even in larger treefall gaps in lowland rainforest. Small and warbler-like, with a white throat, dingy white underparts, a brownish red cap, and brownish upperparts.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Inca Dove
rangeDescription: Semiarid southwestern usa to northwestern costa rica
description: Essentially a ground dove with a long tail. Pale sandy color with scaly pattern covering entire body, unlike Common Ground Dove.

name: Olivaceous Schiffornis
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela, the guianas, and northeastern brazil north of the amazon river
description: Shy, furtive bird that is heard far more often than seen. Shaped like a large manakin; mostly plain greenish-brown with unique large-eyed look.

name: Buffy Helmetcrest
rangeDescription: Central andes of colombia (quindío and tolima)
description: Large, short-billed hummingbird found only at extremely high elevations in Colombia’s central Andes. Adult male’s green and blue beard, black and buff head pattern, and shaggy crest make him easily recognizable within his tiny world range.

name: Sumba Jungle Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Sumba (lesser sundas)
description: A drab flycatcher of lowland forest, edge, and scrub. Longish-billed with a rufous tinge to entire upperparts.

name: Siberian Pipit
rangeDescription: Northern to eastern russia in southeastern taymyr peninsula, western siberian plateau, and from eastward of lena river, yakutsk region, and lake baikal eastward to chukotskiy peninsula, commander islands, sakhalin, and kuril islands; winters from japan and korea to southern and southeastern continental asia; recorded westward to israel and turkey
description: Slender and drab songbird of open country. Brownish above with heavy streaking below.

name: Smooth-billed Ani
rangeDescription: West indies, southeastern mexico (quintana roo) and costa rica southward to western ecuador and northern argentina, also galapagos (introduced); formerly southeastern usa (florida, where now rare)
description: Anis are bizarre, coal-black cuckoos with long floppy tails and unique, curiously tall, flattened bills. Smooth-billed occurs in a variety of open and semi-open habitats in tropical lowlands and foothills, typically staying low in shrubs and grasses.

name: Fulvous-headed Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Andes of central bolivia from cochabamba southward to northwestern argentina
description: Colorful brushfinch of upper humid montane forest and open humid scrubland in the Andes from NW Argentina to central Bolivia. Superficially similar to Rust-and-yellow Tanager, but note contrasting yellow malar and lores.

name: White-breasted Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (eastern bahia to santa catarina and northeastern rio grande do sul)
description: Small tapaculo, found close to the ground in the dense understory of humid lowland and submontane forests, where it is usually very hard to see. It is plump with a short tail that is usually held cocked.

name: Slender-tailed Woodstar
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of eastern bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Small, long-tailed hummingbird of NW Argentina and the Bolivian Andes. Prefers humid and semi-humid middle elevation forests, but generally rare and difficult to find throughout its distribution.

name: Crowned Eagle
rangeDescription: Forest of sub-saharan africa
description: A large, boldly-marked, crested eagle with a long tail and broad wings, resembling a massive goshawk. The underparts of the adult are blotched and barred black-and-white; there is also a variable rufous wash across the breast.

name: Rubeho Akalat
rangeDescription: Montane forest of eastern tanzania (rubeho and ukagura mountains)
description: A rather small, demure understory denizen resembling a cross between a robin and a flycatcher. Mostly dull brown above, with an olive-brown crown and richer orange-brown underparts.

name: Red-necked Buzzard
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan and west-central africa; disperses to sahel
description: This is the common buzzard of much of the Sahel in north, west, and central Africa. Typically has a brown back, a dark chest, a black-spotted white belly, and a rufous tail.

name: Goldie's Bird-of-Paradise
rangeDescription: Fergusson and normanby, in d'entrecasteaux archipelago (off southeastern new guinea)
description: A large bird of foothill forests on the southeast islands. Both sexes have a yellow head and yellow eye.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Stub-tailed Antbird
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of western colombia and northwestern ecuador (esmeraldas)
description: Fairly small, chunky, and short-tailed antbird. Male is jet black.

name: Speckled Spinetail
rangeDescription: Southern colombia to northern bolivia, the guianas, and northern amazonian brazil
description: Fairly small, long-tailed reddish-and-tan bird. Light brown body, with reddish tail, wings, and crown, and prominent fine black spotting in the face and breast.

name: Hawaiian Goose
rangeDescription: Upland lava flows of hawaii; introduced to maui
description: A distinctively marked goose with neck feathers that have a peculiar furrowed appearance. Occurs in wetlands, grassy areas, golf courses, montane shrubland, parks, and even lava fields with sparse vegetation.

name: Orange-throated Tanager
rangeDescription: Río marañón drainage in southeastern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) and northern peru (northern amazonas)
description: Unique and beautiful rainforest tanager known only from several remote areas of the eastern Andes in northern Peru and southeastern Ecuador. No other Andean bird has an orange throat, black upperparts, and blue wings.
